ai.headline: Dropbox adds DocSend viewer tracking and marketing contact collection to its privacy policy
ai.summary: Dropbox's updated privacy policy (posted January 17, 2023, replacing the October 2022 version) now says it collects detailed viewing data when people view files through DocSend or Dropbox analytics, including email address, IP address, device identifiers, how long they view content and which parts. When someone views a DocSend or Dropbox analytics file, the file owner also receives that viewer's name, email, device information, and viewing details. Dropbox also says it may collect information when people meet its representatives at events, download materials, or contact staff, and use it for marketing. Other changes mostly rename "Dropbox Business" to "Dropbox Team," add e-signature activity to usage data, and update the Privacy Shield and Google API wording.

ai.headline: Dropbox updates privacy policy, adds recipient analytics and comment visibility details
ai.summary: Dropbox's privacy policy, dated May 30, 2025, replaces its September 2023 version. The main new points: "Your Stuff" now explicitly includes data from connected services; comments you make on a file are shown with your name and email to anyone viewing that file, including logged-out viewers; and the DocSend-specific analytics wording is generalized to any feature that gives content owners viewer analytics, which still shares your name, email, device, and viewing details with the owner.
ai.what_you_can_do: Users can submit a data access or deletion request by clicking the links in the policy (one for users with a Dropbox account, one for those without), or object to processing by emailing privacy@dropbox.com.
